title: Glycine plus N-acetylcysteine: human muscle evidence with an unresolved randomized functional contrast
decision: retain substantive combination-specific human metabolic and functional-trajectory reserve; no demonstrated BUBR1 restoration or nominee replacement

sources.cohort: 24 older randomized (12/12), 12 young separate uncontrolled; week16 active11/placebo12
sources.exposure: glycine100 mg/kg/day + NAC100 mg/kg/day for16 weeks vs alanine200 mg/kg/day
sources.positive: Measured muscle GSH and within-arm grip/gait/chair-rise improvements
sources.critical_limit: Methods plans OAP16 versus OAG16 functional test, but numeric contrast P/CI and interaction inference are not supplied in examined main/supplement. Within-arm significance cannot establish between-arm benefit.
nulls: lean mass and fat mass nonsignificant
HRQoL and glucose-tolerance improvement not demonstrated
native GCLM, pAMPK/AMPK, ATP5A, LC3AB and POT1 comparisons nonsignificant
statistical_limits: Holm correction within each measure, not across all outcomes
aging-hallmark analyses added exploratory after trial completion
no explicit ITT/PP estimand or sensitivity analysis; one active withdrawal after two weeks
no off-treatment durability established in this RCT

BUB1B.scope: Complete scientific mains and supplements examined, not undisclosed/raw-omics absence proof
limits: pH2AX/8OHdG are damage markers, not karyotype/fidelity
bulk PAX7 does not track stem renewal
p16 decrease does not demonstrate senolytic clearance
PINK1 abundance does not establish flux
NCT01870193 primary muscleGSH differs from publication power calculation based on RBCGSH
NCT05041179 first posted after study completion
NCT05041179 enrollment128 conflicts with paper117 randomized/137 including reference young

safety.2023: No attributed supplement adverse events; ALT/AST/creatinine nonsignificant; other nominal lab changes exist. Small selected short study.
safety.2022: No severe events or attributed discontinuation; one highBP withdrawal without demonstrated causation; ALP mid/high higher judged clinically unimportant by authors.

competition: Visible metabolic/function reserve; stronger design than a generic antioxidant rationale. Apply the same within-arm causal caution to niacin open-label strength evidence. No gene-specific restoration, pediatric primary function or MVA ordering established; retain provisional nominees without claiming superiority.
